overview.title: Operational UX for Shared Mobility Services
overview.desc: A UX system focused on critical state communication and decision-making for shared mobility operators.

problem.title: Problem
problem.desc: Operators managing fleets of shared vehicles face a constant stream of status updates, alerts, and decisions. Without a clear visual hierarchy and state management system, critical information gets lost in noise, leading to delayed responses and operational errors.
problem.challenge: Design an interface that makes the right action obvious at every moment.
problem.detailimg: Cognitive overload: critical information gets lost in the noise

process.title: Process
process.title1: Designing for decision-making, not for visualization
process.desc: Starting from the operator's mental model, I mapped the critical states a vehicle or trip can be in, and the decisions each state requires. I then designed a communication hierarchy: what needs immediate attention, what can wait, and what is purely informational.

solution.title: Solution
solution.desc: A mobile-first operational interface with a clear state management system. Each vehicle or trip state has a distinct visual treatment, color, iconography, and typography work together to communicate urgency and priority without requiring the operator to read every detail.
solution.keyPrinciple: Key actions are always reachable within one tap.

interface.title: Interface
interface.desc: The interface reduces the cognitive effort required to triage operational situations. By making state communication visual and immediate, operators can process more situations in less time.

impact.title: Impact & Learning
impact.impactDesc: The system reduces the cognitive effort required to triage operational situations. By making state communication visual and immediate, operators can process more situations in less time, reducing response latency and decision fatigue.
learningItems: Operational UX is not about aesthetics, it is about reducing friction at the moment of decision.
The most important design skill is knowing what to show, what to hide, and in what order.
Designing constraint forced prioritization of signal over noise from the very first frame.

overview.title: Smart Documents
overview.desc1: AI assisted document validation for international logistics.
overview.desc2: Experimental Product Concept, Design Challenge: how AI could reduce manual document verification in logistics operations.

problem.context1: Logistics operations rely on multiple documents such as invoices, packing lists and bills of lading.
problem.context2: Analysts must manually review these documents to verify that critical information matches across files before shipments are processed.
problem.context3: This process involves comparing quantities, weights, product references and invoice numbers across different formats, often including scanned PDFs, photos.
problem.frictionDesc: Analysts must manually compare multiple documents for each shipment. This repetitive process creates bottlenecks and increases the risk of oversight.
problem.riskDesc: Manual validation increases the probability of human errors.

docs.title: Invoice
docs.desc: Contains sensitive billing information that must match shipment and product data across other documents.

docs.title: Packing List
docs.desc: Item descriptions and quantities often use different nomenclatures (kilograms, grams, units), making direct comparisons difficult.

docs.title: Bill of Lading
docs.desc: Records transport and shipment details that must align with both the invoice and the packing list.

docs.title: Analyst Validation
docs.desc: Analysts must manually compare all documents to identify discrepancies, increasing the risk of delays and human error.

product.title: Product concept
product.desc1: Smart Documents is a document intelligence system designed to automatically analyze and validate logistics documentation.
product.desc2: The platform extracts key information from invoices, packing lists, and bills of lading, enabling automated cross-document verification.
product.desc3: This reduces manual analysis while improving accuracy in shipment validation.

features.title: Automated document extraction
features.desc: The system captures key data fields from invoices, packing lists and bills of lading.

features.title: Data Normalization
features.desc: Information is standardized across documents to resolve naming and unit inconsistencies.

features.title: Cross document validation
features.desc: The platform automatically compares quantities, references, and shipment details across documents.

designApproach.title: Design Approach
designApproach.subtitle: How the solution was structured within a 48 hour design challenge.
designApproach.card1desc: Identify the key logistics documents involved in shipment validation:
designApproach.card1goalDesc: determine the data fields required for cross-document comparison.
designApproach.card2desc: Define how the system could automatically extract and structure relevant data fields from documents.
designApproach.workflowDesc: Design a workflow allowing users to quickly detect inconsistencies between documents and confirm or resolve validation issues.

interfaceSolution.title: Interface Solution
interfaceSolution.subtitle: Turning the concept into a functional interface.

slides.title: Document Upload & Processing
slides.desc: Users upload logistics documents such as invoices, packing lists, and bills of lading. The system processes each file and extracts structured data fields automatically.

slides.title: Automatic Data Extraction
slides.desc: Once uploaded, the platform identifies key data fields within each document and structures them for validation. This allows users to review extracted information quickly without manually reading every document.

slides.title: Cross Document Comparison
slides.desc: The system compares key attributes across documents to detect inconsistencies. Fields such as quantity, shipment references, and item descriptions are automatically matched.

learning.title: Impact & Learnings
learning.impactDesc1: Automating cross-document validation could significantly reduce the time required to review logistics documentation.
learning.impactDesc2: By extracting and comparing key shipment attributes automatically, the system enables logistics teams to identify inconsistencies faster and minimize manual verification work.
learning.learningsDesc1: Designing this concept within a 48 hour challenge required focusing on the core workflow rather than building a complete product.
learning.learningsDesc2: The exercise reinforced the importance of structuring complex document validation processes into clear and actionable interface steps.
learningsItems: Prioritizing core workflows under time constraints.

article.title: Why your brand looks great and still costs you double
article.author: By Ray Viera
paragraphs: You have a logo, a color palette, social media with visual consistency, and a website that makes a good impression.

And yet, every time something needs to be produced, a campaign, a post, a deliverable for a client, the process starts almost from scratch. Someone searches for the right file across three different folders. Someone asks if this version of the logo is the right one. Someone waits on approval from whoever always has to approve everything.
The problem is not the visual identity. It is that the brand has no system.

A brand system is not the manual that lives as a PDF nobody opens. It is the set of documented decisions, organized brand assets, and defined processes that let anyone on the team produce with judgment: without asking, without waiting, without redoing.

Without that system, growth has an invisible ceiling. You can land more clients, hire more people, invest more in content, and still feel just as trapped in the operation. Your brand does not scale because your operation is not ready to.
